title: How do you configure producers/consumers for guaranteed delivery (acks=all, retries, transactions, manual offset commit, DLQ)?
shortTitle: Configuring producers and consumers for guaranteed delivery
keyPoints: Guaranteed delivery is a coordinated stack: no single setting provides it alone.
Producer side: acks=all + min.insync.replicas + idempotence + effectively infinite retries bounded by delivery.timeout.ms.
Consumer side: manual offset commit after processing + read_committed isolation if producers use transactions.
A dead letter queue isolates records that can never be processed, so they are not silently lost.
At-least-once plus idempotent processing is the practical shape of exactly-once for most banking systems.
Downstream side effects must be idempotent on a business id so retries and replays do not double-apply.
Any weak link in the chain (acks=1, auto-commit, no DLQ) breaks the guarantee regardless of other settings.

s1_definition.oneliner: Guaranteed delivery is a stack: acks=all plus min in-sync replicas plus idempotence plus retries on the producer, manual commit after processing with read-committed on the consumer, and a dead letter queue for the unprocessable, all working together.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **acks=all** -- producer waits for all in-sync replicas to persist the record; paired with `min.insync.replicas` for true durability.
- **Idempotent producer** -- `enable.idempotence=true` so retries never create duplicates; the default in modern Kafka.
- **Effectively infinite retries** -- set `retries` to max and bound with `delivery.timeout.ms` so transient failures are retried automatically.
- **Manual offset commit** -- `enable.auto.commit=false` with commit after processing, so a crash resumes from the last truly completed record.
- **read_committed** -- consumer isolation level that skips aborted and in-flight transaction records.
- **Dead letter queue** -- isolates records that cannot be processed after bounded retries, so they are preserved, not lost or blocking.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of guaranteeing that every transfer instruction at National Bank of India is never lost and always acted upon. The producer side is like registered post with delivery confirmation: the sender keeps resending until the recipient confirms (acks and retries), and the post office files a copy in multiple vaults before confirming (min in-sync replicas). The consumer side is like the clerk only stamping a form as done after actually completing the work. The dead letter queue is the problem tray for forms that genuinely cannot be processed.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Guaranteed Delivery Stack

  PRODUCER                    BROKER                    CONSUMER
  ┌─────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────┐
  │ acks=all        │        │ RF=3             │      │ auto.commit=false│
  │ idempotence=true│──send─▶│ min.isr=2        │─poll▶│ isolation=       │
  │ retries=MAX     │        │ 3 replicas       │      │   read_committed │
  │ delivery.timeout│        │                  │      │ commit after     │
  │   =120s         │        │                  │      │   processing     │
  └─────────────────┘        └──────────────────┘      └────────┬─────────┘
                                                                │
                                                      ┌────────▼─────────┐
                                                      │ Idempotent       │
                                                      │ processing       │
                                                      │ (keyed on biz id)│
                                                      └────────┬─────────┘
                                                                │ if fails
                                                      ┌────────▼─────────┐
                                                      │ Dead Letter Topic│
                                                      │ (isolate, don't  │
                                                      │  lose)           │
                                                      └──────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Guaranteed delivery in Kafka is a coordinated stack, and any weak link breaks it. On the producer, set acks=all with min.insync.replicas of at least 2, enable idempotence, and set effectively infinite retries bounded by the delivery timeout. On the consumer, turn off auto-commit and commit only after processing succeeds, set isolation to read_committed if producers use transactions, and make processing idempotent on a business id.

Operationally, a dead letter queue isolates records that can never be processed so they are preserved, not lost. The practical shape of guaranteed delivery for most banking systems is at-least-once delivery with idempotent processing, reserving full transactions for atomic multi-write scenarios.

At National Bank of India, the transfers path uses this stack: acks=all with min.isr=2 on RF=3, idempotence on, manual commit after settlement, and idempotent processing keyed on the trade id. Permanently bad records go to a monitored DLT.

Remember one sentence: guaranteed delivery is end to end, and the guarantee is only as strong as its weakest configured link.
